articles.summary: The largest data centers in the US collectively emit an estimated 25.7 million metric tons of carbon emissions annually — almost as much as Denmark, according to a study published in the journal Nature Sustainability. Harvard researchers found 403 data centers used almost 2% of US electricity , with most of the power being generated from fossil fuels. Sites in Iowa, Ohio, and Virginia accounted for about half the estimated emissions. The study provides the first peer-reviewed estimates of emissions generated by US data centers since the start of the AI boom, although it is not a comprehensive inventory. Without a publicly available list of facilities, researchers pieced together information using a commercial dataset, satellite imagery, and data on the power mix supplying each regional electricity grid. The findings are likely an underestimate as they exclude data centers that researchers could not sufficiently verify, as well as facilities that rely on on-site power generation. — Chloé Farand
